patch_description: Builds on the best-performing generation (Kalman constant-acceleration filter + RTS backward smoother + localized hysteresis, score 0.63). Key insight from the recommendations: trend-compensation lead reduces lag_error, but only if the slope used for the lead comes from a denoised source. Prior failure (Gen 16's 66.4 false reversals) came from computing the lead via np.gradient(smoothed), which re-injected high-frequency ripple. Here, I advance each RTS-smoothed estimate along its own Kalman/RTS slope state (smoothed[:,1]) with lead = 0.4 × (window_size//4). Since the RTS slope state is model-smoothed, the compensation adds no new reversals while cutting lag. The localized weak-flip hysteresis stage then cleans up any residual micro-oscillations. Output contract preserved: end-aligned, length n − window_size + 1.
